cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses on Mount Sinai and gives him a message for the Israelites. It covers what they're to do once they enter the land He's giving them. And it starts with a Sabbath.

cards.question: When Israel enters the land, the LORD says the ___ itself must observe a Sabbath to Him.

cards.text: For six years they sow, prune and gather, but year seven is a Sabbath of complete rest for the land. Friend, I sat in a junk drawer doing NOTHING for years, and nobody ever called it a Sabbath.

cards.question: True or false: In the Sabbath year, the farmers can still reap the aftergrowth and gather grapes from the untended vines.
Whatever the land yields on its own during the Sabbath year becomes food. Who gets to eat it?

answers.text: The household and even the wild animals
The widows and orphans of the town

cards.text: Then God has them count seven Sabbaths of years: seven times seven, forty-nine years. After that, a horn sounds throughout the land on the tenth day of the seventh month.

cards.question: The horn sounds on the tenth day of the seventh month. What day is that?

cards.text: That horn kicks off the fiftieth year, the Jubilee, and liberty is proclaimed in the land for all its inhabitants. Every time my old junk drawer slid open, all of us held our breath hoping for a day like THIS.

cards.question: In the Year of Jubilee, each person is to return to his ___ and to his clan.
True or false: Once the Jubilee year starts, Israel goes right back to sowing the land.

cards.text: The Jubilee is holy to them. During it, they may eat only the crops taken directly from the field.
Since land goes back home at the Jubilee, a buyer is really paying for the harvests left until then. And God's rule for buyers and sellers is simple: don't take advantage of each other.

cards.question: More years left before the Jubilee means a ___ price. Fewer years left means a ___ price.

cards.text: Then God says that line again: don't take advantage of each other, but fear your God. Friend, somebody once bought me out of a bin for 25 cents, and honestly? They OVERPAID.

cards.question: True or false: God says that if Israel keeps His statutes and judgments, they will dwell securely in the land.

cards.text: Then God says out loud what they might be wondering: "What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?" Fair question, friend.

cards.question: What's God's answer to the worry about eating in the seventh year?

answers.text: A sixth-year crop big enough for three years
Manna on the ground every morning
Grain bought from the nations nearby

cards.text: That one blessed crop feeds them while they sow in the eighth year, all the way until the ninth year's harvest comes in. That's like baking ONE batch and pulling three trays out of the oven.
Now God gets to the heart of it. The land must not be sold permanently.

cards.question: Why can't land in Israel be sold for good?

answers.text: Because the land belongs to the LORD
Because the land belongs to the priests
Because the land belongs to the tribes

cards.text: Israel lives on the land as foreigners and residents with the LORD, so every property must have a way to be bought back. Friend, you can't sell the apartment you RENT. The landlord would like a word.

cards.question: Say an Israelite falls on hard times and sells some of his property. Who can step in and buy it back for him?

cards.text: But what if he has no one to buy it back? If he prospers later and has enough, he can buy it back himself.

cards.question: To buy his land back, the man counts the ___ since its sale and repays the balance to the buyer.
True or false: If the man never gets enough to buy his land back, it stays with the buyer forever.

cards.text: Then a few special cases. A house in a walled city can be bought back for one full year, and after that it's the buyer's for good. But village houses and Levite houses go back in the Jubilee, and the Levites' pastureland can't be sold at all.
Now God turns from land to people. If a countryman becomes destitute and can't support himself, they're to help him as they would a foreigner or stranger, so he can keep living among them.

cards.question: What does God say not to take from that struggling countryman?

cards.text: No lending him silver at interest, and no selling him food for profit. That's like handing a friend a cookie and then sending him a BILL for the crumbs.
God reminds them He's the LORD who brought them out of Egypt to give them Canaan. Then He gives a law for a countryman who gets so destitute that he sells himself to a fellow Israelite.

cards.question: How must the Israelite who bought that countryman treat him?

answers.text: As a hired worker and not a slave
As a slave for the rest of his life
As a prisoner until he pays up

cards.question: True or false: That countryman works until the Year of Jubilee, and then he and his children go free.
Why does God say the Israelites must not be sold as slaves?

answers.text: They're His servants He brought out of Egypt
There are too few of them to spare
Their fathers made a vow at Sinai

cards.text: Servants could be bought from the nations around them and from foreigners living among them. Those could become property, be passed down to sons and be made slaves for life.

cards.question: True or false: Under these rules, an Israelite could rule harshly over his fellow Israelite.

cards.text: Now flip it around. A foreigner living among them prospers, and a poor Israelite nearby sells himself to that foreigner.

cards.question: Who can buy back the Israelite who sold himself to a foreigner?

answers.text: A relative or the man himself
Only a priest of the LORD

cards.text: They count from the year he sold himself up to the Jubilee, and the price is based on a hired hand's daily wages. This is careful math, friend, and I lose count of my chocolate chips at ELEVEN.

cards.question: Many years left until the Jubilee means a ___ redemption price. Only a few years left means a ___ one.

cards.text: Until then, he's treated like a man hired from year to year. And his foreign owner must not rule over him harshly in Israel's sight.

cards.question: True or false: If no one ever buys him back, the Israelite stays with the foreign owner for the rest of his life.

cards.text: God says it twice: the Israelites are His servants. They're the ones He brought out of Egypt, and He closes with "I am the LORD your God." Keep that apron on, friend, because this teaching isn't done yet.
